newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson gets indication for drug.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson gets indication for drug.

text.p: Johnson & Johnson's Ortho Biotech unit said on Thursday that its PROCRIT drug received marketing clearance to reduce the need for blood transfusions in anemic patients scheduled to undergo elective non-cardiac, non-vascular surgery.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted approval for the new indication on December 23, 1996, a spokeswoman said. The company mentioned orthopedic operations as an ideal use for the drug.
PROCRIT, which is manufactured by Amgen Inc, is currently marketed for the treatment of anemia in certain conditions, the company said.
PROCRIT stimulates the production of red blood cells prior to surgery to counter the effects of blood loss during some operations, Ortho said.
The drug is a genetically engineered version of a natural hormone that stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cels, Ortho said.
PROCRIT can be administered once weekly for three weeks before surgery and on the day of surgery by injection under the skin, Ortho said.
The most common side effects with PROCRIT were fever, nausea and constipation, which were comparable to the incidence of side effects of patients taking placebo, Ortho said.
